· Cause of death: drowning; seawater in the lungs.
· Finger-shaped bruises on the left wrist; a scrape on the right collarbone at rail height.
· The top button of the coat torn off. No alcohol.
· Time of death: 23.30–00.30.
AUTOPSY REPORT

Gianni De Luca’s cabin on the ferry (with the branch chief’s approval):

· In the life-jacket locker, among the jackets, the victim’s inspection tablet in its orange case; on it, 214 photographs of three Caruso Marittima tugs and an unsigned draft report.
· Gianni De Luca’s fingerprint on the case.
· On the last page of the logbook, the line ‘23.45 — strong wind’; that night’s weather record shows no wind in the bay.
· On the captain’s phone at 00.12, to the contact ‘Lorenzo C.’: ‘Done.’

SUSPICIOUS DEATH
BDS Napoli — Quartieri Spagnoli Branch
Procida, off Marina Corricella
Suspicious death — drowning
Fisherman
Captain.
At sea I’m the captain; I know what happens out there.
No.

The tugs’ papers were forged, yes; my signature isn’t on them, but the Carusos’ son-in-law said, ‘This woman doesn’t come back to port.’ I asked for the tablet; she wouldn’t give it. I grabbed her wrist; the rail was low. I put the tablet in the locker; I couldn’t throw it away. Maybe one day someone…
You pushed the woman over the rail.
She’s not on the list. I don’t look at passengers; I look at the sea. It was windy that night, everyone was in the saloon; it’s in my log.
He smooths his moustache with two fingers.
The victim was on your ferry.
I went out to the stern and told a passenger, ‘Come inside, it’s dangerous.’ She dropped the tablet; I picked it up, I was going to give it back. Then… then I don’t know.
Gianni De Luca — interview
Passenger.

Yes! A woman in a blue coat, with an orange tablet. She was at the stern; I was in the saloon, behind the glass. The captain in the white shirt went out and over to her. They said something; the woman pressed the tablet to her chest. Then I went back to my book. When I looked up, the captain was alone. I thought the woman had gone in. But we hadn’t reached the island yet, had we?
She pulls her glasses up by their cord and puts them on.
Was anyone else on the ferry?
I’m just a tourist — I only came to see the island.
Birgit Holm returned to Stockholm the same day. Her daughter wrote: ‘My mother is very shaken; she won’t talk.’

PROCIDA  /  SUSPICIOUS DEATH
On the last ferry to Procida a ship inspector went missing; in the morning she was found in the sea.

56, captain of the night ferry on the Procida route.

Tommaso Scotto

On the morning of 11 October 2030, off Marina Corricella on Procida, fishermen found a woman’s body in the sea: Marta Iacono (38), a ship inspector.

The night before, the victim had boarded the 23.15 ferry from Pozzuoli to Procida. The ferry’s captain is Gianni De Luca, its deckhand Tommaso Scotto. There is a single name on the passenger list: the Swede Birgit Holm.
INCIDENT REPORT
Request the autopsy report
Request permission to search the captain’s cabin
Stern deck of the night ferry. 10 October 23.15 – 00.10.
STERN DECK CAMERA — log transcript

The passenger saw everything from behind the glass; if she wasn’t asked after the camera footage was opened, she went back to Stockholm. The deckhand gave the list and the false wind, the camera the man in the white shirt at the stern. A justified search found the tablet among the life jackets.
The message’s recipient: Lorenzo C. In Napoli nobody asked for the surname.
Procida — October 2030

Ship inspector Marta Iacono was about to report that three of Caruso Marittima’s tugs were operating on forged papers. The ferry company’s owner, the Carusos’ son-in-law, told the captain ‘this woman doesn’t come back to port’. Captain Gianni De Luca kept the victim off the passenger list, sent the deckhand to the engine room, asked for the tablet at the stern and, when she refused, pushed the victim over the rail.
Who killed Marta Iacono?
FILE #051  /  BUBE NAPOLI — QUARTIERI SPAGNOLI
File #051 — Procida
Deckhand.
I throw the lines; the captain gives the orders.

She had a ticket; I tore it. On the quay the captain said, ‘Don’t write this woman down, she’s the company’s guest.’ I didn’t. On the way the captain sent me to the engine room, said, ‘Check the oil pressure, don’t come out for ten minutes.’ The pressure was normal.
He rubs the scar on his chin with his thumb.
Why isn’t the victim on the passenger list?
The captain. Every hour on the hour. In the morning the log said ‘23.45 — strong wind, passengers in saloon’. There was no wind at that hour. The sea was like oil.
Who writes in the logbook?

No one — she fell overboard
